findings.location: top-level required fields and scan/chat/restart/screenshots constraints, lines 7-80
findings.affected_requirement: FR-039 and the release-evidence contract check-state and append-only failure requirements
findings.evidence: The plan and release contract require schema-valid planned, attempted, failed, blocked, and not-run records, including preservation of failed evidence. The schema always requires a fully successful Tier 3 shape: two Repository revisions, 50-150 File Code Units, zero failed high-value seeds, at least one exact Cross-Repository REFERENCES Edge and Uncertainty, at least three Business Logic Documents, usefulPercent of at least 80, citation percent 100, zero disclosure, successful restart booleans, and at least four screenshots. A failed, blocked, pre-gate, or not-run attempt cannot honestly satisfy those fields, so the claimed failure-state contract is not representable and AD-10 failure behavior is not implementable as specified.
findings.correction_outcome: Revise the release evidence design and schema so every lifecycle state has a schema-valid honest representation. Use status-conditioned result sections or separate run-envelope and accepted-release-receipt schemas; require success metrics only for passed final checks, require evidence/reason fields for failed or blocked checks, preserve attempted observations, and keep correction runs append-only under new run identities.

findings.location: environment, check, scan, chat, and restart definitions, lines 21-79 and 88-127
findings.affected_requirement: FR-039, FR-043 through FR-046, SC-010 through SC-013, and AD-10
findings.evidence: AD-10 and the release contract require exact commands, exit codes, provider model/config identity, packet fingerprints, artifact provenance, and proof behind Scan/restart counts. The schema records only a nullable command fingerprint, has no command or exit-code field, has no provider model/config identity, and gives the Scan aggregate no required supporting artifact or query receipt. Generic optional check artifacts do not bind those observations to the asserted counts. Consequently a schema-valid manifest can assert release metrics without the source-traceable evidence required by the specification.
findings.correction_outcome: Extend the plan's closed manifest contract with redacted exact-command records and exit codes, provider model and non-secret configuration identity, required packet-fingerprint/result artifacts, and explicit evidence bindings for Scan counts, exact Edge, Uncertainty, Business Logic Document, Cross-Repository flow, restart, and database-ownership observations. Add conditional schema rules tying passed checks and aggregate release claims to those artifacts.

findings.location: screenshots property and screenshot viewKind definition, lines 80 and 128-139
findings.evidence: The contract requires reviewable real Scan-state, grounded Business-answer, grounded IT-answer, restart, and release-summary views. The schema requires only four screenshots and does not require any specific viewKind, so four duplicate scan-state screenshots satisfy it while all four other required evidence categories are absent.
findings.correction_outcome: Require at least one schema-valid screenshot for every mandatory view category, either with five named required properties or draft-2020-12 contains/minContains constraints for each viewKind, while retaining candidate binding, production-state attestation, hashing, and redaction requirements.
